sentences.text: Chromogisaurus was a small herbivore approximately 2 meters long that could walk on all fours.
The fossil record preserves a partial skeleton missing the skull but including parts of the front and hind limbs, pelvis, and tail vertebrae.
The genus Chromogisaurus was first named by the paleontologist Martín Daniel Ezcurra in 2010, with the only known species named Chromogisaurus novasi.

The genus name Chromogisaurus means "color of the earth" in Greek, referencing the Painted Valley where the fossils were found, while the species name novasi honors the Argentine paleontologist Fernando Emilio Novas.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as PVSJ 845, was discovered in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation.
Chromogisaurus is considered one of the oldest known dinosaurs.
Chromogisaurus is classified as an extinct genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur, and cladistic analysis places it within the basal sauropodomorph family Guaibasauridae.
Within the family Guaibasauridae, Chromogisaurus forms a subfamily called Saturnaliinae with its sister taxon Saturnalia.
Chromogisaurus lived in South America about 220 million years ago during the Carnian age of the Late Triassic, with a time range estimated between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
